title: A thermogenetics protocol for detecting gap junction channels in Drosophila egg chambers
protocol: Prepare 18°C fresh dissecting medium.
Add 100 μL of medium in a 500 μL Eppendorf tube.
Dissect fly ovaries and collect stage 10 egg chambers.
Remove the surrounding tissues from the dissected ovaries.
Pull out the ovarioles from the muscle sheath.
Remove late stage egg chambers (stage 12–14).
Transfer the egg chambers to an Eppendorf tube with medium.
Wash the egg chambers twice with 200 μL of dissecting medium.
Add 4 μL of insulin solution to 196 μL of dissecting medium in a new Eppendorf tube.
Remove the wash medium from the 500 μL Eppendorf tube containing egg chambers.
Add 200 μL of medium with insulin to the Eppendorf tube with egg chambers.
Break one 22 × 22 mm coverslip into two equal pieces by pushing hard in the center on a hard surface.
Add two small drops of medium onto the dish.
Carefully place the coverslip pieces on the Lumox dish for live imaging.
Transfer samples in 90 μL medium to the center of two coverslip pieces.
Cover the sample with a 22 × 40 mm coverslip.
Wick away excess medium with a tissue.
Add small droplets (less than 50 μL) of halocarbon oil 27 carefully to the rims of the coverslip.
Allow the oil to spread and seal the coverslip.
Switch to motorized stage with temperature control module before opening the Zen software.
Set the temperature to 23°C using the temperature control module on the Zeiss 780 microscope.
Select “temperature” control module in Zen software and set the temperature to 23°C.
Switch to a 20× objective lens.
Select “Position” in the “Acquisition” mode then switch to “Locate” mode.
Stage 10 egg chambers using microscope eyepiece by adjusting focal plane.
Add selected stage 10 egg chambers by clicking “Add” in the “position” box.
Adjust the 488 nm laser parameters on the Zeiss 780 microscope.
Switch to “Acquisition” mode on the Zeiss 780 microscope.
Set up imaging parameters for GFP imaging using a 500–550 nm channel.
Use a 488 nm argon laser with 2% power and 2 Airy units pinhole size.
Adjust channel gains to less than 800 on the Zeiss 780 microscope.
Set frame size to “512 × 512” pixels.
Apply averaging to 8 times for optimal signal-to-noise ratio.
Use maximum speed setting on the Zeiss 780 microscope.
Click “Move to” in the “Position” box to move to the first egg chamber.
Click “Live” and adjust focus to the mid-plane of the border cells.
Rotate crop box so that the egg chamber posterior side faces right.
Acquire single section image at 23°C.
Repeat steps for moving to, focusing, and acquiring images on subsequent egg chambers.
Set the temperature in the “temperature” module to 32°C after imaging all egg chambers at 23°C.
Wait for the air temperature to stabilize at 32°C, which typically takes about 10 min.
Repeat steps 12–14 to acquire the same single section image in 32°C.
Use the lowest laser power and exposure time that allow visualization of the sample to prevent photobleaching.
Measure background in a nurse cell region using a “Rectangular selection” box without selecting the follicle cells.
Open the image in FIJI.
Use “Analyze->Histogram” to obtain the background mean and standard deviation.
Choose pseudo color and adjust image for display.
Use the adjusted image to measure the intensity in follicle cells.
Calculate background value as "mean+3 × StdDev."
Select the entire image.
Subtract background value using “Process->Math->Subtract” function.
Save the image as “file name_remove background.”
Duplicate the image using “Image->Duplicate” function.
Create binary mask by adjusting threshold to select bright signal in duplicated image.
Divide mask by 255 to create a 0/1 binary mask image.
Save the mask as “file name_mask.”
Multiply the mask with original image using “Process->Image Calculator” to obtain a new image.
Save the image as “file name_remove background_masked.”
Duplicate the image again using “Image->Duplicate” function.
Change lookup table in duplicated image to visualize dynamic range in different color coding.
Use “Image->Adjust->Brightness/Contrast” to adjust the brightness/contrast.
Save the 32-bit image in tiff format.
Convert the image to an RGB image and save it for display.
Select ROIs of follicle cells using the “Freehand selections” function.
Measure the intensity using the “Analyze->Measure” function.
Export the data and use the “Mean” intensity for further analysis.
Summarize and plot the result.
Calculate changes in GCaMP6s intensity as ΔF/F0.
Import ΔF in control and experimental group in Prism 6 GraphPad.
Plot the data and perform statistical analysis.
